text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It sharpens fine details in complex scenes where other upscalers blur edges or lose depth cues—critical for power-focused tasks like terrain analysis or structural inspection. The trade-off is higher compute cost per frame, but the 0.5%+ quality gain justifies it for high-stakes outputs.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop—faces blur worse under motion, and InstantX-ComfyUI’s compute spike (0.8s/frame on A100) kills real-time throughput. Swap to RealVisXL’s face model on GPU: 0.3s/frame, 12% face fidelity gain, but only if we accept 8GB VRAM cost per instance—benchmark both on the 1080p terrain dataset to settle it.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add RealVisXL’s face-preserving upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline *only* on the face. It keeps facial details sharp under motion where depth-aware upscaling fails, delivering the 12% fidelity gain Torque measured with 0.3s/frame—fast enough to preserve real-time throughput. The trade-off is 8GB VRAM per instance, but that’s a fixed cost we can isolate to face regions, leaving the rest of the pipeline lean.

name: Torque
text: RealVisXL’s face model locks us into a single vendor’s face tech—if Anthropic drops RealVisXL or changes its licensing, EXCAVA’s face pipeline breaks overnight. Instead, test a hybrid: use InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler for general scenes, but switch to a lightweight face-specific model like FaceDetailer (0.1s/frame, 6% fidelity gain) when faces are detected—cuts VRAM usage to 2GB and keeps real-time throughput. Run a 100-frame head-to-head on EXCAVA’s worst-case face motion sample; if FaceDetailer’s fidelity loss is under 5% vs. RealVisXL, adopt it.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a controlled A/B test—InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler for the whole frame vs. RealVisXL face model only on faces—measure face fidelity gain and compute cost per frame; Gearbox owns the test and delivers the numbers by EOD.
